title: BTEC National Extended Diploma Applied Science (2016) — selected Unit 15

handoff.scope: Inventory and generation/extraction requirements only. No symbol geometry, device models, footprints or application subfolder feature is implemented.
handoff.folder_semantics: folder is a proposed slash-separated logical path, not a claim of support in the current TinyCAD library browser.
handoff.source_document_base: All source_document paths are relative to the repository root, including in standalone library files.
handoff.identity: id is stable within a library; extraction may deduplicate by canonical_symbol_id, but each library is complete and permits independent duplicate assets.
handoff.pin_contract: Logical terminal numbers and signal names are not physical package pinouts. Resolve real package pins from an authoritative device reference before generating package-specific symbols.
handoff.conventions: Prefer IEC/UK teaching symbols. Power pins and polarity should remain explicit. Built-in instruments, probes, independent waveform sources and voltage-controlled sources are excluded from symbol generation. Use existing_tools configuration with the native tool defaults.
handoff.existing_tools: existing_tools and existing_tool_ids refer to supplied non-library tools, not generation requirements. Never recreate these as library symbols.
handoff.inventory_not_bom: One record per reusable symbol type, not per component instance. A bridge can be assembled from repeated diode/resistor symbols. Different resistance/capacitance values are properties, not separate symbols.
handoff.model_warning: Every record is marked not ready to simulate from this manifest. A successful extraction of artwork does not establish a valid model, mapping or instrument implementation.
handoff.optionality: experiment_symbol_ids are a coverage set of proposed implementations and comparisons, not a minimal mandatory BOM; common support symbols and explicitly optional additions are separately identified.

experiments.title: Resistor networks
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare up to three resistors in series, parallel and mixed arrangements. Record equivalent resistance and conductance, with calculations beside the schematic.

experiments.title: Meter positions and loading
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare a divider with different voltmeter input resistances and current-meter burdens. Document which quantity each connection measures.

experiments.title: Potential-divider design
experiments.catalogue_description: Choose a target output and vary resistor ratio. Add a finite load and quantify the change rather than assuming an unloaded formula remains exact.

experiments.title: Emf and internal resistance
experiments.catalogue_description: Use an ideal source plus a series resistor. Change the load and fit terminal voltage against current using exported values. Identify the declared model's emf and resistance.

experiments.title: Ohmic/non-ohmic behaviour
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare resistor and LED characteristics using DC sweeps. Use a suitable electrothermal lamp model if including a filament lamp; a constant resistor cannot reproduce heating.

experiments.title: Capacitor reservoir and transferred charge
experiments.catalogue_description: Capture charge and discharge currents and capacitor voltage. Integrate current over a selected interval and compare with the voltage change.

experiments.title: Capacitors in series and parallel
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare networks using the same charging resistance. Infer equivalent capacitance from a transient response; the student multimeter has no capacitance range.

experiments.title: Capacitor filtering
experiments.catalogue_description: Apply a sine or pulse to an RC network. Compare input/output amplitude and timing across frequencies and relate the result to the chosen component values.

experiments.title: Peak and RMS readings
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a low-voltage sine source, scope and AC meter. Compare readings over complete cycles and distinguish a source's offset from its alternating component.

experiments.title: AC-to-DC supply stage
experiments.catalogue_description: Prepare a rectifier with compatible diodes and a smoothing capacitor. Vary load and capacitance; compare mean output and ripple from transient captures. This is an electronic implementation of the topic, not a complete mains-supply model.

experiments.title: LDR interface
experiments.catalogue_description: Enter measured sensor resistances for several illumination conditions and predict divider output. Optical distance/intensity must come from measurements or a declared model.

experiments.title: Thermistor interface
experiments.catalogue_description: Use measured R(T) values to compare output sensitivity and sensor placement. Keep the temperature calibration separate from the electrical prediction.

experiments.title: Strain-gauge bridge
experiments.catalogue_description: Model the bridge resistors and sweep a small declared resistance change. Measure differential output and the effect of an initially unbalanced bridge. Mechanical strain is not generated by the solver.

experiments.title: Reed-switch alarm interface
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw the switched input, bias resistor and indicator. Compare separate switch states or a compatible controlled switch. Magnetic actuation is external to the circuit.

experiments.title: Thermocouple readout and amplification
experiments.catalogue_description: Supply measured thermocouple voltages through a stated source resistance. Test loading and an amplifier interface. The model does not independently reproduce thermoelectric conversion.

experiments.title: Piezoelectric sensor interface
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a justified charge/current-source and capacitance equivalent. Compare output pulses and loading. The mechanical excitation is a declared input.

experiments.title: Sensor/data-logger connection plan
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw the sensor, conditioner, supply, common reference and recorder interface for a selected physical measurement. TinyCAD does not stream data into a real logger or model every pH/moisture/pressure sensor.

experiments.title: Model-versus-measurement evaluation
experiments.catalogue_description: Repeat a selected circuit with nominal and measured component values. Keep predicted and bench data separate, then identify discrepancies attributable to loading, tolerance or an inadequate model.
